Contributing to plancap

Source: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md

Thank you for helping. Three kinds of contribution are especially welcome.

1. A rulebook for a new jurisdiction

plancap is built so that adding a jurisdiction needs no package code: only a rulebook and the jurisdiction’s zoning layer. If you have entered one, please share it.

  • Every value needs a source: the plan, chapter and rule it comes from. A number without a source cannot be checked.
  • Use the highest limit that is still permitted (or its local equivalent of “as of right”). Where the plan allows open-ended breaches at a discretionary status, use the stated standard.
  • Record every rule you could not model in unmodelled_rules, with the likely effect of modelling it (overstates, understates or either).
  • Run validate_rulebook() before opening a pull request.

2. A rule the package cannot yet express

Open an issue with the Rule not supported template. Quote the rule text, link the plan, and say how it is measured. A diagram helps a great deal.

3. Bugs and code

  • Open an issue with a minimal reproducible example, ideally on exampleton().
  • For pull requests: one change per pull request, a test that fails before and passes after, a NEWS.md bullet, and devtools::check() clean.
  • Code style follows the tidyverse style guide. Geometry code must not loop over sites with GEOS calls inside; use spatial indexes and grouped operations.

Code of conduct

Please note that this project is released with a Contributor Code of Conduct. By contributing you agree to abide by its terms.
